transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-01
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Martinez (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Laura Kim (Willow CTO); Ravi Singh (Lead ML Engineer); Maria Gonzales (IT Security); Ethan Park (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for onboarding. Discussed goals, data residency, SSO, deployment options and initial timeline. Assign action items and schedule follow-ups.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um i'm ava from redwood, i'm the account executive on this. quick intros?
[00:12] Laura Kim: hi this is laura, cto at willow creek, thanks for doing this.
[00:18] Ravi Singh: ravi here, i'll be leading the ml integration and benchmark testing.
[00:22] Maria Gonzales: maria from it security. we'll focus on compliance and network.
[00:26] Ethan Park: ethan product, i'll be tying the rollout to our roadmap.
[00:30] Diego Martinez: diego, solutions engineer at redwood. happy to own the tech deep dive.
[00:35] Priya Nair: priya, customer success, i'll be your onboarding lead.

[00:48] Ava Chen: great, thanks. high level goals for this kickoff: confirm success criteria, decide on hosted vs dedicated vs private, map security requirements and timeline for pilot. laura, what's top priority for willow?
[01:05] Laura Kim: speed to market is big, we have a compliance-sensitive dataset that we'll process so data residency and audit logs are musts. ideally start with a pilot by late feb, pilot should prove latency under 200ms for common flows and cost per request is reasonable.
[01:28] Ava Chen: okay that's helpful. ravi, technical constraints?
[01:32] Ravi Singh: most of our traffic is short chat-like requests, a 2k token context occasionally. we also have an existing inference infra for embeddings and some reranking. primary concerns are latency and predictable p99s. we can try hosted first but if we hit variability we may move to dedicated or private.
[01:52] Diego Martinez: gotcha, those are common patterns. quick note: our dedicated pools give you predictable throughput and isolation. private/vpc option is available for data residency but setup adds lead time.
[02:10] Maria Gonzales: from security, we need SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs retention for 12 months, SOC2 & ISO artifacts, and the ability to rotate keys via our KMS. also network allowlisting, ip ranges.
[02:29] Priya Nair: perfect, we'll collect the SSO metadata and the onboarding checklist. ava i'll send the security questionnaire and SOC2 links after this call.

[02:42] Ethan Park: timeline wise, a feb pilot is tight, can you outline the minimum steps?
[02:48] Ava Chen: yes. step one, set up staging project and SSO. step two, run a small eval set & benchmark with diego and ravi. step three, iterate on batching and quantization recommendations to hit cost targets. final step, production roll after acceptance. roughly 4-6 weeks.

[03:12] Ravi Singh: quick Q, how do you handle kv cache and prefix caching? our chat model relies heavily on cached context.
[03:20] Diego Martinez: we do prefix/KV cache, yes. small hiccup: sometimes paperwork transcribes it as k v cash in our tools, but the runtime keeps the kv cache across sessions where applicable. caching reduces per token cost and improves latency for repeated prefixes.
[03:37] Laura Kim: cost question: how do you surface token-level costs during testing?
[03:42] Priya Nair: console shows token-level cost and latency breakdown, and we'll provide sample dashboards. you can also tag routes to break out costs per feature.

[04:00] Maria Gonzales: on private deployments, do we have to be on-prem or can we do VPC with cloud region control?
[04:08] Diego Martinez: VPC is the common approach—private control plane with customer-managed networking—on-prem is an option but more effort. you can pin model versions and we support key management integrations with your KMS/HSM.

[04:28] Ava Chen: any competitors you're evaluating?
[04:31] Laura Kim: we looked at anthro—anthropic—and openai for hosted. also an in-house team looked at self-hosting some models.
[04:42] Ava Chen: noted. we can share a side-by-side on throughput and unit economics.

[04:50] Diego Martinez: for the benchmark plan, i propose an initial suite: small chat flows (50-200 tokens), large contexts (~2k tokens), and embeddings throughput. we'll measure p50/p90/p99 latency and tokens/sec on both hosted and a small dedicated pool.
[05:10] Ravi Singh: sounds good. what env do you need for dedicated testing? images or api keys?
[05:16] Diego Martinez: we can provision a dedicated pool in staging; we'll need service account keys and ny ok to open network for a short time for the bench harness. we'll coordinate exact IPs.

[05:36] Maria Gonzales: we'll need an architecture diagram and list of flows to review for compliance. are those docs available?
[05:43] Priya Nair: yes i'll share the onboarding deck and the security pack right after this.

[06:00] Ethan Park: integration: how do we do feature flags / gradual rollouts?
[06:06] Diego Martinez: console supports canary rollouts, A/B testing and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant if we hit errors. also you can control routing policies by latency/cost/region.

[06:26] Laura Kim: can we set autoscale policies? we don't want unexpected spend.
[06:31] Ava Chen: yes, dedicated pools have autoscaling policies with cap and burst options; plus you can set quotas in the console to cap spend. we'll document recommended settings.

[06:50] Ravi Singh: one more: quantization—any guidance for our workload?
[06:55] Diego Martinez: we recommend model-by-workload quantization; small chat flows often tolerate 4-bit quantization, but we'll run cost-quality tests during the benchmark.

[07:10] Laura Kim: ok. let's talk timeline concrete: can we aim for pilot start week of feb 22?
[07:18] Ava Chen: that's reasonable. so next two weeks: we get SSO set up, staging provisioned, and initial security docs exchanged. the diego-ravi deep dive week of feb 8 to define bench. pilot run week of feb 22.

[07:36] Maria Gonzales: action: i'll send the approved ip ranges and any firewall rules.
[07:40] Maria Gonzales: also note, we need contract language around data retention—who owns logs and how they are deleted.
[07:48] Ava Chen: we'll surface that to legal; priya i'll follow up with procurement.

[08:00] Priya Nair: i'll kick off the CSM project and invite the stakeholders; you'll see invites today.

[08:05] Ava Chen: recap of owners: ava sends onboarding + security pack; diego coordinates bench with ravi; priya sets up project and staging; maria sends ip ranges.

[08:22] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, practical question: during pilot who will be our primary support contact?
[08:27] Priya Nair: i'll be your day-to-day CSM, and diego will be on-call for technical issues; ava handles account and procurement.

[08:38] Ravi Singh: ok thanks. one small note, in our infra we use a custom Okta setup and we need sample SAML metadata files.
[08:47] Ava Chen: i'll include an Okta SAML template and step-by-step SSO guide in the pack.

[09:00] Laura Kim: any open risks we should document now?
[09:03] Diego Martinez: lead time for private/vpc provisioning is biggest risk if you require dedicated on-prem. also initial latency tuning may require a few iterations.
[09:12] Maria Gonzales: legal and contract changes re data retention could delay procurement.

[09:20] Ava Chen: great. last bit—do we want a recurring weekly check-in during pilot?
[09:25] Laura Kim: yes weekly syncs please. same time wednesdays preferred.
[09:29] Priya Nair: i'll set up recurring wednesdays 15:00 UTC starting 2027-02-23.

[09:36] Ava Chen: perfect. thanks all, i'll send the pack and next steps.

[09:40] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., kv cache -> k v cash) typical of auto-generated exports. References: onboarding checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/wch), SOC2 pack (link noted in follow-up).
